source: GitHub (euan-forrester/save-file-converter issue #80, 'Idea: Genesis Everdrive <-> MiSTer save conversion', comment of 2022-03-02 23:18 UTC)
author: birdybro (MiSTer documentation maintainer): 'here's just a big zip of all my saves on my MiSTer for you now so you can see'
licence: none stated (a file attached to a public GitHub issue)
what_it_is: birdybro's save from the MiSTer WonderSwan core, member WonderSwan/Another Heaven - Memory of those Days (Japan).sav of saves.zip (MiSTer's saves/WonderSwan folder). 2 KiB (16 Kbit) cartridge EEPROM, stored as little-endian 16-bit words + 512-byte clock sector = 2560 bytes. Clock record time 2021-06-05 22:31:28 UTC. The EEPROM starts 34 12 (word 0x1234).
note: Origin: the poster's description of the zip plus the core's own clock sector, which no other emulator writes. Most of the ~80 WonderSwan saves in the zip were written one to two minutes apart that evening, so the game was probably only booted far enough to create or initialise its save; nothing in the thread says how far each was played. The last 512 bytes are the core's clock sector: one 16-byte record repeated 32 times, 'TR' (the constant "RT" written as a little-endian word), then 10 bytes holding the 42-bit RTC_savedtime and the 32-bit Unix time of the save (WonderSwan.sv time_din_h = {32'd0, time_din, "RT"}), then 4 zero bytes. The core appends this sector to every save, clock cartridge or not (has_rtc = 1'b1). The zip also holds MiSTer saves for other systems (GBA, Genesis, SNES, PSX, TGFX16, Lynx, MegaCD, NEOGEO, ...), not used here.
